gloss: on top of that; to make matters worse; besides

definitions.gloss: on top of that; to make matters worse; besides
definitions.explanation: Adds further information, often something that compounds or worsens an already described situation.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り、おまけに{風|かぜ}も{強|つよ}かった。
examples.english: It was raining, and on top of that, the wind was strong.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}に{乗|の}り{遅|おく}れた。おまけに{財布|さいふ}も{忘|わす}れた。
examples.english: I missed the train. On top of that, I forgot my wallet too.

examples.japanese: {渋滞|じゅうたい}で{遅刻|ちこく}した。おまけに{大事|だいじ}な{書類|しょるい}を{家|いえ}に{置|お}いてきてしまった。
examples.english: I was late because of traffic. To make matters worse, I left important documents at home.

notes:
A conjunction used to pile on additional information, typically something negative or undesirable that compounds the preceding statement. While it can appear with positive additions, it is most naturally used when listing unfortunate or inconvenient circumstances.

USAGE:
- Typically begins a new sentence or follows a comma
- Most natural when the added information makes the situation worse
- Can also be used for neutral or positive additions, but this is less common

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- おまけに{雨|あめ}まで{降|ふ}ってきた: on top of that, it even started raining
- おまけに{熱|ねつ}まで{出|で}た: to make matters worse, I even got a fever
- おまけに{道|みち}にも{迷|まよ}った: besides, I also got lost

SIMILAR WORDS:
- しかも: moreover — similar meaning but more neutral in tone; used for both positive and negative additions
- その{上|うえ}: furthermore — slightly more formal; used in writing and speech
- さらに: in addition — formal and neutral; common in written Japanese
- {挙句|あげく}の{果|は}てに: and to top it all off — stronger emphasis on a final, often worst outcome
